theme: Hannah’s prayer; Samuel born and given; Eli’s corrupt sons
readingInstruction: Read 1 Samuel 1:1-2:36. A new book begins, and it starts with a barren woman at a sanctuary. Read Hannah’s prayer in chapter 2 slowly, and notice how it looks far beyond her own situation.
settingTheScene: The book of Judges ended with the words, “In those days there was no king in Israel. Everyone did what was right in his own eyes.” The books of Samuel pick up the story at that low point. The priesthood is corrupt, the nation is scattered, and the ark is at Shiloh. 1 and 2 Samuel were originally one book, and they tell how Israel moved from the judges to the monarchy, and how God chose David. The story begins with one woman’s prayer.
observation: Elkanah has two wives. Peninnah has children, and Hannah, whom he loves, has none, and Peninnah provokes her (1:1-8).
Hannah prays in bitterness of soul and makes a vow: if God gives her a son, she will give him to the LORD all his life (1:10-11).
Eli the priest thinks she is drunk, then blesses her, and “her face was no longer sad” (1:12-18).
Samuel is born, and when he is weaned, Hannah brings him to Eli at Shiloh: “For this child I prayed” (1:20-28).
Hannah’s song begins, “My heart exults in the LORD; my horn is exalted in the LORD” (2:1).
“There is none holy like the LORD: for there is none besides you; there is no rock like our God” (2:2).
“The LORD kills and brings to life… He raises up the poor from the dust” (2:6-8). The song ends with “his king” and “his anointed” (2:10).
Eli’s sons, Hophni and Phinehas, “were worthless men. They did not know the LORD” (2:12), and a man of God announces judgment on Eli’s house (2:27-36).
interpretation:
The opening scene is quiet and domestic, yet it sets the tone for the whole book. God works through the weak. Hannah is barren and humiliated. The priest misjudges her. The nation is corrupt. Yet from this pain comes the prophet who will anoint Israel’s kings. It echoes Sarah, Rebekah, and Rachel, the barren mothers of Genesis, and it shows that God’s plan often begins where human strength has run out.

Hannah’s prayer is honest and costly. She does not hide her bitterness. She pours out her soul before the LORD. And she vows to give back what she asks for. When Samuel is weaned, she keeps her vow, and she leaves her only son at the sanctuary. The gift is real, and it is received in joy: she worships rather than grieves.

Her song in chapter 2 is the theological center of the section, and it announces the theme of the whole book. The LORD reverses human expectation. The mighty are broken, the feeble gird on strength, the full hire themselves out for bread, the barren bear seven. “He raises up the poor from the dust.” The song ends by looking forward to “his king” and “his anointed.” Hannah does not yet know that Israel will have a king, but she already sees that God’s kingdom turns the world upside down.

Against this stands the failure of Eli’s house. His sons take the sacrificial meat by force and sleep with the women who serve at the tent. Eli rebukes them gently, but he does not restrain them. The prophecy against his house shows that God will not be mocked in his own sanctuary. He will raise up a faithful priest.

The chapter sets two houses side by side. One is a house of prayer and faith, and the other is a house of privilege and corruption. The LORD honors those who honor him, and those who despise him will be lightly esteemed.
connection: Mary’s Magnificat in Luke 1:46-55 echoes Hannah’s song closely, with its themes of the mighty brought down and the lowly lifted up. Hannah is the first to speak of God’s “anointed” (the Messiah) in the Bible. Jesus, like Samuel, grew in “favor with the LORD and also with man” (2:26; Luke 2:52). Paul says that “God chose what is foolish in the world to shame the wise” (1 Corinthians 1:27).
application:
Bring something you are bitter about to God honestly, as Hannah did.

Read Hannah’s song aloud. Ask which line you most need to hear.

Think about what you have been given that you could dedicate back to God.
prayerPrompts: Pray honestly about something you have been holding back from God.
Thank him for lifting the poor from the dust.
Ask him to help you give back to him what he has given.
